# bobina — full documentation for agents

> Generated by tools/gen_llms_full.py from the files below; the index is llms.txt.


<!-- file: README.md -->

# bobina

Print Markdown on thermal roll printers — receipts, lists, labels, QR codes, payment codes (Pix, UPI, SEPA…), photos —
with calibrated defaults, a preview you can trust, and **nudges instead of blocks**.

```bash
bobina print "# MARKET\n- [ ] milk\n- [ ] bread"
bobina print list.bob.md
bobina template new receipt sale.bob.md && bobina print sale.bob.md
```

Every command that prints shows a **confirmation screen** first (the dry run): a terminal preview
on the real 32-column grid, paper length, counters it will use, and nudges with the evidence
behind them. `p` prints; `--yes` skips it. **Without a terminal (scripts, agents, ssh) add `--yes`**:
otherwise nobody can answer and the print stops with `E107` (exit 7). `-n` shows the screen and prints nothing.
Agents: start at [llms.txt](llms.txt) (or [llms-full.txt](llms-full.txt), everything in one file); a ready skill
is in [skills/bobina/SKILL.md](skills/bobina/SKILL.md).

```
┌─ preview · mtp-ii-58 · 58 mm ──┐
│                                │
│M A R K E T                     │
│                                │
│☐  milk                         │
│☐  bread                        │
└────────────────────────────────┘
 ~3.1 cm of paper · 1 native rows, 2 raster · 2.9 KB
 [p] print   [s] save as…   [q] quit
```

## Why

Cheap 58/80 mm printers are good enough for a lot — if something takes care of their limits.
bobina was calibrated on a minimum-quality printer (Goldensky MTP-II): every default comes from
a printed and photographed test, so what works there works on better printers. You can ask for
anything; bobina only warns, and tells you why (`warning[Q101] … (evidence: N6)`).

- **One engine** for check, preview and print: the PNG preview is the exact dot pattern sent.
- **Native when the printer does it well, raster when it does not** — per line, decided by the
  printer profile (glyphs the font lacks, italic, inverted bands, drawn checkboxes).
- **Readable documents**: plain Markdown plus Pandoc-style attributes. See [docs/FORMAT.md](docs/FORMAT.md).
- **Safe data**: values from CSV or `--set` are printed literally and can never inject Markdown,
  template code or printer commands; templates run in a sandbox.

## Install

```bash
curl -LsSf https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rafaelbressan/bobina/main/get.sh | sh   # installs uv if missing
# or: uv tool install bobina · pipx install bobina · a .deb or Homebrew: docs/INSTALL.md
bobina init                   # printer, profile, locale, roll, test strip
bobina init --yes             # agents, scripts: no questions, no print
```

Bluetooth printing needs Linux and the system Python (`get.sh` picks it). The .deb, pipx, the boot service and a
checkout: [docs/INSTALL.md](docs/INSTALL.md).
Printer on another machine? `bobina init --command "ssh tower bobina send --yes -"`. No printer at hand?
`bobina init --yes --printer ./out.bin`: every job's bytes are appended to `out.bin` (a file printer).
Dates and money: the first `check`, `preview` or `print` takes the locale from the time zone and saves it
(`M203`); `bobina config set locale en-US` changes it.

## The format in one screen

````markdown
---
locale: pt-BR
counters:
  ticket: { start: 1, format: "A-{:03}" }
fonts:
  body: native                 # the printer's own font (fast)
  hand: Z003                   # any alias you like
---
# TICKET {{ seq.ticket }} {.invert .center}

{{ now | date("full") }}        <!-- quinta-feira, 5 de novembro de 2026 -->

- [ ] open task
- [x] done task (struck)

| Item | Qty | Price |
|---|--:|--:|
| Bread | 6 | {{ 4.8 | currency("BRL") }} |

```qr
https://example.com
```

```pay {scheme=pix to="you@example.com" name="Shop" city="Rio" amount=10.00}
```

Signed, [Ana]{font=hand size=32px}

--- {.cut}
````

`bobina help format` has the rest: sizes (`small`…`huge`, physical mm), dividers, barcodes,
Data Matrix, PDF417, images (dither and gamma), rotation, upside-down text, templates and data.

## One label per row

A document with `{{ blanks }}` plus a table (CSV, TSV, JSON, Excel) prints one label per row; the
columns fill the blanks. Step by step: [docs/guides/batch-printing.md](docs/guides/batch-printing.md);
in the terminal: `bobina help data`.

```bash
bobina check jar-label.bob.md --data pantry.csv                 # paper length, problems, the columns: no print
bobina print jar-label.bob.md --data pantry.csv --where shelf=A --copies-from jars --yes  # jars=0: no label
bobina print tag.bob.md --data stock.xlsx --sheet Estoque --yes  # a sheet other than the first
bobina print shelf-tag.bob.md --data a=prices.xlsx --join b=catalog.json --on name --yes  # {{ a.price }} {{ b.id }}
bobina print note.bob.md --set produto=Feijão --set validade=2027-01-31 --yes   # one value, no table
bobina preview jar-label.bob.md --data pantry.csv -o 'labels/{product}.png'    # one PNG per label
```

A `{{ name }}` that is not a column prints empty and is reported (`M130`, with the columns the data has).

## Commands

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `print [FILE \| "TEXT" \| -]` | render → confirm → print. `--data rows.csv` (above), `--set KEY=VALUE`, `--copies N` (identical), `--repeat N` (new counter values each), `-o job.bin` (save, do not print); stops after each label (`--no-step`) |
| `print --last` / `--again` | reprint the last job: identical bytes / re-rendered (new `now` and counters); with `-o FILE` save instead |
| `check FILE` | problems, paper length, native/raster rows, nothing printed (`--data`, `--json` → `{"stats", "problems"}`, `--strict`) |
| `preview FILE \| "TEXT"` | exact PNG (`-o out.png`); `--data rows.csv -o 'dir/{column}.png'` one per label; `--realistic` simulates ink spread |
| `view FILE` | preview in the terminal |
| `edit [FILE] [--template NAME]` | write in your editor, confirm, print |
| `template list \| show \| new` | receipt, label, todo, card, note, and a shop gallery: [guides/templates.md](docs/guides/templates.md) |
| `seq list \| set \| reset` | persistent counters (`{{ seq.NAME }}`); `seq set ticket 100`: the next print uses 100 |
| `init` | first run; again to change one part |
| `printer scan \| add \| list \| use \| remove \| show \| set` | printers live in `~/.config/bobina/config.toml` |
| `config list \| get \| set \| unset \| edit` | the other settings (`config set step off`) |
| `status`, `mode [esc\|tspl\|cpcl]` | printer state; command language |
| `calibrate compare PHOTO FILE` | how close the preview is to the paper |
| `calibrate tear` / `calibrate feed` | where the tear bar is; whether feeds after images need the safe mode |
| `paper [new 15m \| used 3m]` | paper left on the roll (the printer only reports "out") |
| `profile list \| show`, `fonts list`, `send FILE.bin` | profiles, tested fonts, raw bytes |
| `mcp` | a server for AI agents (MCP; `uv tool install 'bobina[mcp]'`, then `claude mcp add bobina -- bobina mcp`): [docs/mcp.md](docs/mcp.md) |

`bob` is the same binary. Short aliases exist for typing (`bobina help aliases`); docs always use
full names. Exit codes: 0 ok · 1 usage · 2 document · 3 strict nudges · 4 unreachable · 5 printer
not ready · 6 language · 7 confirmation needed/declined · 8 security · 9 a payment or contact code left out (Q111,
Q112) · 10 newer release.

## Repository

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `src/bobina/` | the package (engine, layout, ESC/POS, preview, CLI) and built-in profiles, templates, fonts |
| `docs/` | [`FORMAT.md`](docs/FORMAT.md) (the `.bob.md` spec), [`CLI.md`](docs/CLI.md) (commands, options, problems, exit codes), [`SECURITY.md`](docs/SECURITY.md) (threat model), [`guides/batch-printing.md`](docs/guides/batch-printing.md), [`TESTED.md`](docs/TESTED.md) (what was and was not tested on paper) |
| `examples/` | documents and data used by the guides (`examples/batch/`) |
| `spec/conformance/` | test tickets with expected bitmaps — a `bob/1` implementation renders them identically |
| `tests/` | unit, security and golden tests (no printer needed) |
| `docs/printers/` | measured capabilities of each profiled printer (`mtp-ii-58.md`) |
| `contrib/` | Bluetooth boot service for Linux (`install.sh` sets it up) |
| `tools/` | maintenance scripts: public export and personal-data scan |

## Status

Pre-release (v0.x). MIT licensed (bundled fonts keep their own licenses: `src/bobina/fonts/LICENSES.md`). Baseline profile: `mtp-ii-58` (measured); 32 more imported from escpos-printer-db, not measured on paper (`bobina profile list`; calibrate before trusting them). Realistic preview is an estimate until
the profile is calibrated from photos (`preview.calibrated = false`).

## Hardware notes (MTP-II)

| Symptom | Likely cause |
|---|---|
| `printer unreachable` | printer off or asleep: press POWER until the yellow LED is steady |
| Blank output | roll upside down (the side that darkens with a fingernail faces the head) |
| Turns off when printing | battery: charge it; first use: remove the film on the battery contacts |
| Prints garbage | another app sent a different command language (TSPL/CPCL) as text; the MTP-II itself only speaks ESC/POS |
| Self-test | printer off → hold FEED, press POWER, release at the beep |
| The last line stops at the tear bar, or a `--marks tear` line is off | `bobina calibrate tear` (a ruler: tear it and read the mm), then `bobina calibrate feed` (does the printer obey a paper feed right after an image?) |


<!-- file: docs/agents.md -->

# bobina for agents

bobina is made to be run by programs and AI agents as well as by people: every print shows a confirmation screen,
every problem has a code, and every command that returns data has `--json`.

## The four rules

1. **No terminal, add `--yes`.** `bobina print FILE --yes`. Without it nobody can answer the confirmation screen
   and the print stops with `E107` (exit 7). `print -n` shows the screen and prints nothing.
2. **Look before paper.** `bobina check FILE` (paper length and problems), `bobina view FILE` (the preview in the
   terminal), `bobina preview FILE -o out.png` (the exact image). Print only what the user asked for.
3. **Read the codes.** Warnings never block: each one has a code, a suggestion and the evidence. `bobina help CODE`
   says what to do; [problems/README.md](docs/problems/README.md) lists every code.
4. **Try without hardware.** `bobina printer add test --path out.bin` is a file printer: each job's bytes are
   appended to `out.bin`.

## Machine output

- `bobina check FILE --json` (and `print`, `preview`) gives `{"stats", "problems"}`; `--problems json|jsonl`
  writes problems to stderr. Schemas: [schemas/README.md](docs/schemas/README.md).
- `bobina help --json` describes every command, option, topic and problem code.
- Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 usage, 2 document, 3 strict, 4 unreachable, 5 printer not ready, 6 language,
  7 confirmation, 8 security, 9 a payment or contact code left out (`Q111`, `Q112`), 10 a newer release (`bobina update --check`). [CLI.md](docs/CLI.md#exit-codes) has the table.
- Servers, bots and cron: `BOBINA_NONINTERACTIVE=1`, one process per job
  ([CLI.md](docs/CLI.md#long-jobs-and-limits)).

## Files for agents

- [llms.txt](llms.txt): the index, with the facts an agent needs first; [llms-full.txt](llms-full.txt): the
  docs in one file.
- [skills/bobina/SKILL.md](skills/bobina/SKILL.md): a ready skill (when to print, what never to do).

## The MCP server (`bobina mcp`)

`bobina mcp` gives agents bobina as tools (check, preview, print with `confirm: true` after the user agreed,
paper): setup and the tool list in [mcp.md](docs/mcp.md).


<!-- file: docs/CLI.md -->

# bobina — CLI conventions (draft v0.4)

Language: **English everywhere** (messages, help, docs, spec).

## Principles

1. **Agnostic core, opinionated defaults.** Anything the user asks for explicitly is executed as asked. Calibrated defaults (from the printer profile) only fill in what was not specified.
2. **Nudges, not blocks.** Warnings go to stderr with a suggestion and the evidence behind it; they never stop a print. `--quiet` silences them, `--strict` turns them into errors (CI/automation).
3. **What you check is what you print.** `check`, `preview` and `print` share one engine. Every printing command accepts `--dry-run`.
4. **Nothing prints without confirmation.** Every command that prints shows the confirmation screen first and waits for `p`. `--yes` (`-y`) skips it, explicitly.
5. **Readable by humans and agents.** Full command names are canonical. Human-readable output by default, `--json` on every command that returns data, stable exit codes.
6. **Discoverable.** `bobina help`, `bobina <command> --help`, `bobina help format`, `bobina help data`, `bobina help pay`, `bobina <thing> list`,
   `bobina help E302` (what a problem code means and what to do; docs/problems/), `bobina help --json` (the CLI for
   programs). JSON outputs have schemas in docs/schemas/.

## Names

- Binary: **`bobina`**. `bob` is an installed alias of the same binary.
- **Canonical form is always the full command name** (`bobina print`, `bobina check`). Docs, help text, examples, error messages and anything generated by the tool use full names only.
- Short aliases exist purely as typing shortcuts for interactive use, are documented in one place (`bobina help aliases`) and are never shown elsewhere.

## Commands

| Command | Does | Alias |
|---|---|---|
| `print [FILE \| - \| "TEXT"]` | render, confirm and print a `.bob.md` document, inline text, or stdin; `--last` reopens the last confirmation | `p` |
| `check FILE` | lint: line breaks, truncated words, unsupported glyphs, paper length, black coverage, nudges | `c` |
| `preview FILE -o OUT.png` | exact bitmap, or `--realistic` (calibrated dot gain) | `pv` |
| `view FILE` | preview in the terminal (block/braille characters) | `v` |
| `edit [FILE] [--template NAME]` | write in your editor → confirmation screen → print | `e` |
| `status` | paper / cover / error / language mode; `--list` explains every state; file and command printers: none (exit 0) | `s` |
| `mode [esc \| tspl \| cpcl]` | show or switch the printer command language | `m` |
| `send FILE.bin` | send raw bytes untouched (escape hatch) | — |
| `fonts list \| test \| mark \| scripts \| get` | recommended fonts, the font test registry; fonts for other scripts (`get thai`, `get hi`, `get menu.bob.md`: download now, offline later) | — |
| `seq list \| set \| reset` | persistent counters used by `{{ seq.NAME }}` | — |
| `init` | first run: printer, profile, locale, roll, a test strip with the calibration ([below](#first-run-init)) | — |
| `printer scan \| add \| list \| use \| remove \| show \| set \| unset` | find and store printers; `set NAME KEY VALUE` | — |
| `config list \| get \| set \| unset \| edit` | every setting and its value (`--all`: advanced too); `edit` checks the file; a bad value is a note, never a stop | — |
| `profile list \| show \| use` | printer profiles | — |
| `template list \| show \| new` | ready-made documents (receipt, label, todo, card, shop tags…) | — |
| `calibrate compare\|tear\|feed` | photo vs preview; tear bar distance (ruler); feeds after images (3 lines) | — |
| `help [COMMAND \| format \| nudges \| aliases]` | help | — |
| `mcp` | a server for AI agents (Model Context Protocol): [mcp.md](docs/mcp.md) | — |
| `chat`, `ai` | an AI whose answers print: [chat.md](docs/chat.md) | — |

Everyday use: `bobina print "buy bread"`, `bobina print list.bob.md`, `echo "hi" | bobina print --yes`.

## First run (`init`)

`bobina init` finds the printer (Bluetooth, USB, a file, ssh), confirms its profile and the locale, asks the
roll (as `paper new`), then offers one test strip with the calibration and asks what the paper shows. Run again to
change one part. `--yes` (or `BOBINA_NONINTERACTIVE`) asks and prints nothing: the first printer found
(`--printer` chooses), its profile, the locale; the roll stays unset (`P104`). `--json`: `bobina.init/1`.
`--printer` takes a name from `bobina printer list`, a Bluetooth address, a device (`/dev/usb/lp0`), a file for a
test printer (`--printer ./test.bin`) or the name a printer nearby gives itself.

## Confirmation screen

Shown by every printing command (it is the dry run):

```
┌─ preview · mtp-ii-58 · 58 mm ────┐
│ MARKET               05/11/2026  │
│ ☐ milk                           │
│ ☐ bread                          │
└──────────────────────────────────┘
 ~7.2 cm of paper · 4 native blocks, 1 raster
 seq.ticket: will use A-042 (reserved for this print; given back if it is not printed)
 warning[F204] line 3: font "Z003" at 16px is illegible → use ≥ 28px  (evidence: F1-16)

 [p] print   [e] edit again   [s] save as…   [q] quit
```

- Enter alone never prints.
- `print --last` reopens the confirmation of the last document (identical content, same reserved values); `--again` re-renders it (new `now`, new `seq`).
  With `--yes` either one prints at once and says where (`reprinted on loja: ~1.5 cm (identical bytes)`); with
  `-o FILE` it saves the bytes to that file instead and prints nothing (`--again -o` spends no seq numbers).
- No terminal attached (pipes, cron, agents) and no `--yes` → shows the confirmation on stderr, prints nothing, exit code 7.
- `--copies N`: N identical copies. `--repeat N`: N renders, each with new counter values. The screen shows the total ("10 tickets: A-042 to A-051").

## Drafts and editor (`edit`)

```
bobina edit                        # blank draft
bobina edit --template receipt     # draft from a template (fields prefilled, # required / # optional)
bobina edit list.bob.md            # existing file (or create it)
```

- A draft is a full `.bob.md` (front matter, variables, counters, templates), stored in `~/.local/state/bobina/drafts/`; the last one is kept for `print --last`.
- Drafts start with a column ruler as an HTML comment (exact for the native font only; the preview is the truth).
- Editor: `--editor CMD` > config `editor` > `$VISUAL` > `$EDITOR` > `nano` > `vi` (Notepad on Windows).
- GUI editors return immediately unless told to wait; bobina adds the flag for known ones (`code`/`cursor --wait`, `subl -w`).

## Inline text is an implicit document

`bobina print "TEXT"` (and stdin) is treated exactly like a `.bob.md` file with that content: same parser, same check, same nudges.

- `--plain` disables Markdown (prints the text literally, still word-wrapped).
- `\n` in the argument is a newline (typing multi-line text in a shell is awkward): `bobina print "# MARKET\n- [ ] milk"`.
- Backslash before a Markdown character escapes it, as in CommonMark (`\*`, `\#`).
- `check` warns when text looks literal but would be interpreted (e.g. a lone `*`, `#` without a space, a log line starting with `---`).

## Batches (`--data`)

One design with `{{ blanks }}` + a table whose columns have the same names = one label per row. Step by step,
with pictures: [`docs/guides/batch-printing.md`](docs/guides/batch-printing.md).

## Saving instead of printing (`-o`)

`-o FILE` (`--output FILE`) saves instead of printing. An existing FILE is replaced only with `--force`, and a file
the job reads (document, image, data) is never replaced. Without `-o`, `preview` writes `DOCUMENT.preview.png`. In `print` it saves the bytes the printer would get (any
name; `.bin` by convention), to send later with `bobina send`. In `preview` it saves the picture of the strip:
`.png`, `.jpg`, `.pdf`, `.webp`, `.bmp`, `.gif` or `.tif`, chosen by the extension.

**One file per label**: put a placeholder in the name (like ffmpeg's `frame%04d.png`):

| Placeholder | Becomes | Needs data? |
|---|---|---|
| `{n}`, `{n:03}` | label number in the whole job: 1, 2 … / 001, 002 … | no |
| `{i}`, `{i:02}` | number inside its document (restarts for each file) | no |
| `{file}` | document name without the extension (`jar`, `cover`) | no |
| `{part}` | the `--then` part | no |
| `{column}`, `{b.column}` | a value of that row (`{item}` → `rice`) | yes |
| `{column\|slug}` … | the value in another case: `lower`, `upper`, `slug`, `snake`, `kebab`, `camel`, `pascal`, `deaccent`, `titlecase` | yes |

```
bobina preview a.bob.md b.bob.md -o 'out-{n}.png'                     # out-1.png out-2.png
bobina preview cover.bob.md --then jar.bob.md --data kitchen.csv -o 'out/{file}-{i:02}.jpg'
bobina preview jar.bob.md --data kitchen.csv -o 'tag-{item}.png'      # tag-rice.png …
bobina print jar.bob.md --data kitchen.csv -o 'jar-{n}.bin'           # each file is a whole printable job
bobina preview jar.bob.md --data kitchen.csv --pages -o batch.pdf     # one PDF, one page per label
```

Values from data are cleaned for file names (`../../x` cannot leave the folder; `/ \ : * ? " < > |` become `_`).
Two labels that would get the same name are an error (add `{n}` or `{i}`); existing files are replaced only with
`--force`; a missing `{column}` lists the available names. Folders in the name are created.

## Label by label (`--step`)

A print of several labels stops after each one, so you can tear it off:

```
 ✓ 3/10 printed: tear it off
 [Enter] next (4/10 · Honey)   [a] all 7 left   [r] again   [s] skip   [q] stop
```

`r` reprints the last (same number), `q` says how to print the rest (`--rows 4-10`); unprinted labels give
their numbers back. Only at a terminal with a real printer: not with `-o`, a file printer, agents or `--yes`
(unless `--step` is written). `--compact` prints at once (`P105`). `--no-step`: this print at once; `--step 3`:
stop every 3; `bobina config set step off`: always at once.

## One strip (`--compact`, `--then`, several files)

Every label normally ends with the feed to the tear bar, so you can tear each one off. To print several things as
one job — one preview, one confirmation, one paper count — give several files, or split the command into
**parts** with `--then`:

```
bobina print a.bob.md b.bob.md @shelf                        # three documents, one job
bobina print jar.bob.md --data kitchen.csv --compact \
  --then jar.bob.md --data laundry.xlsx --sheet Laundry \
  --then receipt.bob.md --no-compact --compact-all
```

**Rules** (like ffmpeg: options belong to the part they are written in; the specific beats the general):

1. A **part** is everything between two `--then`: one or more files and their options (`--data`, `--where`,
   `--copies-from`, `--set`, `--ask`, `--page` …). The options apply to every file of that part.
2. `--compact` / `--no-compact` set a part; `--compact-all` is the default for every part. Both flags in one part
   is an error.
3. **Joins**: inside a compact part, labels are glued at a ✂ cut. Between two parts there is a ✂ cut only if
   **both** are compact; otherwise the paper feeds to the tear bar. The end of the job always feeds.
4. Job options (the table below) may be written in any part. Counters (`{{ seq.x }}`) continue across parts and
   files; copies of a row repeat its number.

The terminal preview always draws where one label ends: `┄┄ ⟶ ┄┄` where the
paper goes to the tear bar, `✂ ┄┄┄` at a cut.

**On paper, no mark by default** (a cut is just space). To see on the strip where one order ends and the next
begins, `--marks cut` prints a fine dashed line (1 dot, 4 on / 4 off) at every cut, `--marks tear` prints it so
that the final feed leaves it on the tear bar (it uses the `tear_mm` measured by `bobina calibrate tear`; 5 mm
without one), `--marks both` does both; `bobina config set marks both` makes it the default. The marks change
no length, and the confirmation screen says which ones go on paper.

| Command | Strip (⟶ tear feed, ✂ cut line) |
|---|---|
| `a b --then c d --compact` | A ⟶ B ⟶ C ✂ D ⟶ |
| `a b --then c --then d --compact` | A ⟶ B ⟶ C ⟶ D ⟶ (D's neighbour is not compact) |
| `a b --then c --no-compact --then d --compact-all` | A ✂ B ⟶ C ⟶ D ⟶ |
| `jar --data kitchen.csv --compact --then jar --data laundry.xlsx` | jar 1 ✂ jar 2 ✂ jar 3 ⟶ jar 4 ⟶ jar 5 ⟶ |

**Which options belong where** (tested in `tests/test_strip_rules.py`):

| Kind | Options | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Part | `--set`, `--data`, `--sheet`, `--rows`, `--where`, `--copies-from`, `--repeat`, `--copies`, `--ask`, `--page`, `--plain`, `--allow-net`, `--allow`, `--compact`/`--no-compact` | apply to the files of the part they are written in, never to the next part |
| Job flag | `--compact-all`, `--sandbox`, `--yes`, `--dry-run`, `--strict`, `-q`, `--json`, `--no-color`, `--step`/`--no-step` | may be written in any part, apply to the whole job |
| Job default | `--set-all KEY=VALUE`, `--allow-all CODES` | every part gets them; a part's own `--set`/`--allow` wins |
| Job value | `--printer`, `--profile`, `-o`, `--editor`, `--marks` | one value per job; two different values are an error |
| Not with documents | `--last`, `--again` | reprint the last job; an error with targets or `--then` |

**Errors and warnings in a long job.** Every part is built and checked before the printer is touched, and every
problem is reported at once, in one format (the same in every command):

```
3 errors, 1 warning — nothing printed
✗ error   part 2 (nope.bob.md): file not found: nope.bob.md
✗ error   part 4 (jar.bob.md): --where: no column 'color' (columns: item, n)
✗ error   [M310] part 5 (bad.bob.md): templates cannot read files (include/import are disabled)
! warning [I101] part 3 (photo.bob.md), line 3: image 'missing.png': No such file or directory
            → paths are relative to the document
```

One error anywhere and nothing prints; the exit code is the most serious one (security 8 > document 2 > usage 1).
Warnings never stop the job by themselves: on the confirmation screen you decide (`p` prints without the missing
image, `q` gives up); with `--yes` they are shown and the job prints anyway; with `--strict` any warning stops
everything (exit 3), also with `--yes` (`--yes` only skips the confirmation screen). So either the whole strip prints or nothing does. Literal text `--then` cannot be printed:
it always separates parts. `--dry-run` shows the whole strip (up to 12 labels on
the terminal; `bobina preview -o strip.png` has all of them) and every warning; the confirmation screen shows the
same before `p`. Only one part can read stdin (`-`).

Several targets are files, `@names`, images or URLs; plain words are refused (`bobina print hello world` →
use quotes: `bobina print "hello world"`). `--last` reprints a multi-part job as it was; `--again` re-renders
only single documents. The tested cases are in `tests/test_strip_rules.py`.

## Saved labels (`library`, `@NAME`)

Labels printed often are saved once and printed by name, without opening an editor:

```
bobina library add shelf shelf-label.bob.md --note "pantry shelf"
bobina library add bread "# BREAD\nbest before {{ today | add(days=3) | date }}"
bobina library list                         # @shelf  pantry shelf  fields: item (--set or --ask)
bobina print @shelf --set item=Rice         # or --ask; preview and confirmation as usual
bobina library show shelf · bobina library rm shelf
```

An entry is a snapshot in `~/.config/bobina/library/` plus the folder it came from, so relative images keep
working; `@NAME` works anywhere a FILE does (`print`, `check`, `preview`). Names are letters, digits, `.`, `_`
and `-`: never paths. `--force` replaces an entry.

## Filling a template on the terminal (`--ask`)

```
$ bobina print --ask receipt.bob.md
Fill in the fields (Enter = default / leave empty):
shop (required) e.g. Padaria do Zé: Padaria do Zé
items (required) - list of [item, quantity, unit price]
  one row per line: item; qty; price  (empty line to finish)
  1> pão; 2; 1.50
  2> café; 1; 4
  3>
currency - ISO 4217 code [BRL]:
date [automatic]:
```

Only the fields still missing are asked; answers are literal data, like `--set`. Then the usual preview and
confirmation follow.

## Images, SVG and PDF as the target

`bobina print photo.jpg`, `bobina print logo.svg`, `bobina print label.pdf --page 2` (or `--page 1-3`; default: all
pages, one image per page) build a one-image document and go through the same preview and confirmation. Vector
files are rendered at the paper width and thresholded (crisp text and lines). Typical use: export a label from
another app (Dlabel, a browser, Office) as PDF and print it with bobina's calibration.

A file is recognized by its content, not only its name. Anything else (Word, Excel, PostScript/EPS, binary
files, a broken image) is refused with the list of supported formats and a hint to export as PDF: printing it
would waste paper on garbage, so this is an error, not a nudge. Inside a document the same problems are
nudges (`I101`) and the rest prints; a document with nothing left to print adds `L105`.

`bobina print https://… --allow-net` does the same for an https image. Network images are off unless the command
line says `--allow-net`, never from a document by itself; private and local addresses are refused (see
`docs/SECURITY.md`). `--sandbox`: a shared document's images only from its folder and `image_dirs` (config.toml, `I108`).

## Shape

```
bobina [global options] <command> [arguments] [command options]
```

Global options:

| Option | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--profile NAME` | printer profile (default: configured; base `mtp-ii-58`) |
| `--printer ADDRESS` | target device (default: from config/profile) |
| `--quiet` | no nudges |
| `--strict` | nudges become errors (exit 3) |
| `--json` | structured output |
| `--dry-run` | never touch the printer |
| `--yes`, `-y` | print without the confirmation screen |
| `--verbose` / `--debug` | more detail / dump bytes sent |
| `--no-color` | no color (also honors `NO_COLOR`) |
| `--help`, `--version` | |

Short flags are allowed only for the most common options (`-o` output, `-q`, `-n` dry-run, `-y`, `-h`) and, like command aliases, are never used in docs or generated output.

Configuration precedence: **flag > document front matter > `~/.config/bobina/config.toml` > profile > built-in default**.

<!-- 'Help layout' left out here: see docs/CLI.md -->

## Lists

Pattern: `bobina <thing> list` — table for humans, `--json` for machines.
`bobina status --list`, `bobina fonts list`, `bobina profile list`, `bobina template list`, `bobina help nudges`.

## Nudges

Flow of warnings, refusals and prints: [`docs/diagrams/nudges-flow.md`](docs/diagrams/nudges-flow.md).

One format on stderr, with a stable code so they can be filtered or allowed:

```
warning[B101] line 12: 1px stroke prints broken on profile mtp-ii-58 → use 2px  (evidence: R4-01)
warning[F204] line 3: font "Z003" at 16px is illegible → use ≥ 28px or Atkinson 16px  (evidence: F1-16)
```

- Code = category + number: `B` drawing, `F` font, `Q` barcodes/QR, `L` layout, `I` image, `P` printer, `M` markup.
- Always: where, what, suggestion, evidence (the test id that justifies it).
- `--quiet` silences all; `--allow B101,F204` (or front matter `allow: [B101]`) silences specific ones.

## History (`bobina history`)

Every `bobina print` is recorded, whatever happens: printed, cancelled, failed, saved (`-o`), dry run or stopped by
`--strict`. One JSON line per job in `~/.local/state/bobina/history.jsonl` (schema `bobina.history/1`): id, time,
duration, outcome and exit code, printer and profile, labels, length, ✂ cuts and tear feeds, the parts (file names),
counters used, every problem (same fields as `--problems json`) and the sha256 of the bytes sent.

```
bobina history                              # newest first, one line per job (like git log --oneline)
bobina history --long --limit 5             # every detail
bobina history --outcome failed --since 2026-11-01
bobina history show last                    # or an id, or the start of one
bobina history stats                        # jobs by outcome, labels, paper per week, frequent problems
bobina history --json · bobina history clear --yes
```

Private by default: the text of labels is not kept; on the stored command line, inline text becomes `text`,
`--set`/`--set-all`/`--where` keep only the key (`KEY=***`, they can be a Pix key or a phone number) and option
values are kept only for file and number options. Problem messages are stored with every value given to the job,
long digit runs and e-mails replaced by `***`. Abbreviated options are refused, so none slips past this. `bobina config set history off` turns it off;
`history_max` (default 5000) bounds it.

## Problems: one format, four renderings

Every error, warning and note has a code from the catalog (`bobina help nudges`; errors are `E1xx`–`E5xx`) and
the same fields. `--problems` (any command; or `BOBINA_PROBLEMS`) chooses how they are written to stderr:

| Format | For | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `pretty` (default) | people | `! warning [I101] part 3 (f.bob.md), line 3: image 'missing.png' …` + `→ hint` |
| `plain` | grep, scripts | `warning I101 part 3 (f.bob.md) line 3: image 'missing.png' … -- hint` |
| `json` | one document | `{"outcome": "nothing printed", "problems": [ … ]}` |
| `jsonl` | logs | one object per problem per line |

Fields (schema `bobina.problem/1`): `code`, `severity` (`error`/`warning`/`note`), `message`, `suggestion`,
`line` (in the document, or null), `evidence` (the printed test behind a limit), `outcome` (`nothing printed`,
`printing anyway (--yes)`, `nothing printed (dry run)`, `nothing saved` for preview, empty for check and view …)
and, in multi-part jobs, `source`, `part` (number) and `file`. Exit codes are below; the most serious problem decides it.

The problems always go to **stderr**, so stdout stays free for the data of the command: `--problems json > f`
saves the human summary, not the JSON. To keep the problems of a document in a file, use `check --json`, which
writes them to stdout in the same shape, next to the paper figures:
`bobina check doc.bob.md --json > problems.json` → `{"stats": {…}, "problems": [ … ]}`. `print --json` and
`preview --json` write the same, next to what happened (`outcome`, `exit`, `saved_to`; `files` for preview): one
object on stdout, schemas in docs/schemas. `view`, `edit`, `send`, `mode` and `mcp` write no data: there `--json`
does nothing and a note says so.

## Two commands at the same time

Two terminals, a script and the tower over ssh may run bobina at once. Its own files stay whole:

- **seq numbers** never repeat (see FORMAT.md, counters): each print reserves its numbers under a lock.
- **One job per printer.** A second print waits for the first ("waiting for the printer: another bobina job is
  using it…") instead of fighting for the Bluetooth link. After `busy_timeout` seconds (printer entry in
  `config.toml`, default 300) it stops with `E405` and nothing is sent. `bobina status` during a print answers
  `E405` at once.
- **Paper, history, saved labels, config, --last**: every change is made under a lock and written whole (temporary
  file + rename), so a reader never sees half a file and two changes never lose one another.
- **A damaged file is an error, not a fresh start** (`E209`, with the file name): an empty `counters.json` would
  restart the numbering. bobina never overwrites it; fix it or move it away. The paper odometer only advises: a
  damaged `paper.json` is shown on the confirmation screen and the print goes on.

## Long jobs and limits

- **Previews of long strips are split.** Above ~2.5 m (20000 dots) one image does not open in most viewers:
  `preview -o tira.png` writes `tira-1.png`, `tira-2.png` … and says so. Each page is drawn and saved on its own
  (one page in memory); previews are 1-bit PNGs.
- **`--last` keeps the exact bytes and the preview of the labels the terminal showed** (up to 12), not a drawing of
  the whole job.
- **Nothing waits forever.** A download has 20 s in all (DNS included), a device file (`transport = "file"`) and
  a `command` printer have `timeout` (printer entry, default 120 s), `bluetoothctl` calls are bounded. stdin takes
  up to 10 MB (a document), `bobina send -` up to 64 MB.
- **Servers, bots, cron: `BOBINA_NONINTERACTIVE=1`.** bobina never asks on the terminal: `--ask` and the
  confirmation stop at once with `E107` (pass `--yes` and `--set`); the notice before a font download is the
  note `F304` in the problems, never a terminal line. Also give the target explicitly and start
  bobina with stdin closed (`stdin=DEVNULL`): with no target, bobina reads a document from stdin.
- **One process per job.** bobina keeps some settings per process (problem format, Pillow's image size limit,
  caches), so call it as a command, not as a library from several threads. A server runs one `bobina`
  subprocess per job (`start_new_session=True`), behind a queue per printer; that also bounds the memory of each
  job.

## Agents

Agents and the files written for them: [agents.md](docs/agents.md); the MCP server `bobina mcp`: [mcp.md](docs/mcp.md).

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | ok |
| 1 | usage error |
| 2 | document error (parse) |
| 3 | nudges with `--strict` |
| 4 | printer unreachable / Bluetooth; `fonts get` could not download |
| 5 | printer error state (no paper, cover open) |
| 6 | printer language mismatch (e.g. printer in TSPL, document needs ESC/POS) |
| 7 | confirmation required (no terminal and no `--yes`) or declined |
| 8 | security error (template sandbox violation, see FORMAT.md §7) |
| 9 | the job went out (printed, saved, shown) without a part it exists for: a payment or contact code that was not built (`Q111`, `Q112`). The rest printed; `--allow Q111,Q112` makes it 0 |
| 10 | `bobina update --check`: a newer release exists |

## Install and files

- Install and upgrade: [INSTALL.md](docs/INSTALL.md) (`bobina update`).
- Config: `~/.config/bobina/config.toml` (`bobina config list`).
- Profiles: built-in + `~/.config/bobina/profiles/*.toml` (`bobina profile show NAME`).
- State (counters, drafts, last print): `~/.local/state/bobina/`.
- Downloaded fonts for other scripts: `~/.local/share/bobina/fonts/` (`BOBINA_DATA_DIR`); `bobina config set font_downloads off` (or `BOBINA_FONT_DOWNLOADS=0`) turns automatic downloads off.

<!-- 'Decided' left out here: see docs/CLI.md -->

## Implementation notes

- Printers: `transport = bluetooth` (status checked before printing: exit 5 if cover open/paper out), `command`, `file`.
- Confirmation is read from `/dev/tty`, so `cat x | bobina print` still asks.
- The last print is kept in `~/.local/state/bobina/last/` (`--last`, `--again`).
- **Calibration** (also on the `init` strip): `bobina calibrate tear` prints a ruler with no feed after it; the mm at
  the torn edge (`bobina calibrate tear 5`) + 6 mm (`tear_margin_mm`) ends every job. `bobina calibrate feed`: lines
  A–B 10 mm drawn, B–C a 10 mm ESC J right after B; `touching` (the MTP-II) keeps the safe mode, `apart` turns it
  off. **Safe by default**: an unmeasured printer sends feeds after images as white rows, waits until idle
  at the end (per-printer keys `blank_rows_after_raster`, `idle_before_tail`).
- **What a profile turns on** (`bobina profile show NAME` lists it). Three features follow the ESC/POS spec and are
  tested on the bytes only; a job that uses one gets the note `P301` (docs/TESTED.md):
  - Code pages: `encoding = "codepage"` and a `[codepages]` table (codec = `ESC t` number, in order of preference):
    accented text stays native, switching page where a character needs it. **⚠ not tested on paper.** With
    `encoding = "utf-8"` (the MTP-II) text goes as UTF-8; with `"ascii"` only ASCII is native, the rest raster.
  - Automatic cutter: `cutter = "full"` or `"partial"` cuts (`GS V`, where the paper is) after the final feed of each
    label; `--compact` labels stay glued, to be cut by hand.
    **⚠ not tested on paper.** `bobina calibrate tear` then measures the distance to the blade.
  - Native barcodes on imported profiles (`barcode.native` from the printer database). **⚠ not tested on paper.**
- `calibrate compare` finds the paper in the photo, scales it to the printable width and reports length error, row-profile correlation and a 0–100 score, plus a side-by-side PNG (exact | realistic | photo).
- `bobina paper`: a paper odometer per printer. `paper new 15m` (`1500cm`, `50ft`; or `--diameter 40mm --core 12mm --thickness 0.06`) when a roll is loaded, `--width 57mm` to warn (`P103`) when the roll is narrower; a package code (`57x30`) is refused with a question; every confirmed print adds its length; the confirmation shows the metres left, `P101` when the roll is almost over (< 1 m or 10%), `P102` when the print is longer than what is left. `paper used 3m` sets the total used, `paper used +30cm` adds to it (prints from other apps, raw `send` jobs and the self-test are not counted). On "paper out" the error suggests `paper new`.


<!-- file: docs/FORMAT.md -->

# The `.bob.md` format — `bob/1` (draft v0.4)

Status: **draft**. Becomes `bob/1` once frozen. Every feature below is marked
**✓ implemented** (in bobina v0.1, covered by tests) or **◇ planned** (part of the format, not implemented yet;
using it gives the note `M103` or `M102`, never an error).

A `.bob.md` file describes a print for a thermal roll printer. It is valid Markdown — it reads well on GitHub
or Obsidian — and it maps predictably onto narrow, low-resolution printers.

## 0. Principles

- **Plain Markdown first.** Any Markdown file is a valid `.bob.md`.
- **Readable over terse.** Names are full English words (`invert`, `align=center`), never codes.
- **Reuse standards.** CommonMark + Pandoc-style attributes for markup, Jinja for variables, Unicode CLDR for
  dates and numbers, BCP 47 for languages, IANA for time zones.
- **The document says what, the printer profile says how.** Native command or raster, dots per millimetre and
  every limit come from the profile, so the same file prints on 58 mm and 80 mm, 203 and 300 dpi.
- **Nudges, not blocks.** Anything questionable prints with a warning that carries a suggestion and the test
  that justifies it. Only security violations stop a print (§9).
- **What you check is what you print.** The preview is the exact dot pattern sent to the printer.

File extension: **`.bob.md`** (canonical); `.bob` is accepted. Encoding: UTF-8.

## 1. Front matter (optional) ✓

```yaml
---
bob: 1                         # format version (informational for now)
profile: mtp-ii-58             # printer profile; the CLI or the printer config can override it
locale: pt-BR                  # BCP 47: month names, numbers and money, all in it (`lang:` too); default: the machine's (§7.1)
timezone: America/Sao_Paulo    # IANA; default: the system zone
align: left                    # default alignment: left | center | right | justify
size: normal                   # default text size (§5)
fonts:                         # font roles and aliases (§4)
  body: native
  title: native
  code: IBM Plex Mono
  hand: Z003
image: { dither: floyd-steinberg, gamma: 1.8 }   # photo defaults (§6.5)
tasks: { done: strike }        # strike (default) | check | plain (§2)
counters:                      # persistent sequences (§7.3)
  ticket: { start: 1, format: "A-{:03}" }
allow: [F301]                  # nudge codes accepted for this document (silenced)
template: receipt              # fill a template (§8); the other keys become its fields
labels: { pt: { total: Total } }   # override a template's fixed labels
---
```

Every key is optional. Any other key is a **variable** available to the body (`shop: Padaria` → `{{ shop }}`).

## 2. Markdown ✓

| Markdown | Result |
|---|---|
| `#`, `##`, `###` (and deeper, styled as `###`) | headings in the **printer font**: 2×2 bold, 1×2 bold, bold (profile `native.headings`); a raster font with `fonts.title` |
| paragraph | word-wrapped by bobina, never by the printer (the printer splits words) |
| a newline inside a paragraph | a **line break** (as in Obsidian), not a space |
| `**bold**` `*italic*` `~~strike~~` `` `mono` `` | inline styles; italic and strike are drawn as raster on printers without them |
| `- item`, `1. item`, nested lists | bullet `•`, right-aligned numbers; nested items and continuation lines align under the item text |
| `- [ ] todo`, `- [x] done` | drawn checkboxes; done items struck through. `tasks.done: check` = box only, `plain` = `[ ]`/`[x]` in the printer font (fastest) |
| `\| a \| b \|` tables | monospace grid, header bold with a rule under it, column alignment from `:--`/`--:`, **stretched to the paper width** (the first column absorbs the slack); `{.compact}` keeps it narrow |
| `---` | divider (§3) |
| `> quote` | `│ ` prefix |
| `![alt](photo.jpg){…}` | image (§6.5) |
| `<!-- comment -->` | ignored |
| `\*`, `\#` … | CommonMark escapes: the character is printed literally |

## 3. Attributes `{…}` ✓

Pandoc syntax: `.class`, `key=value`, `key="quoted value"`. They go:
- at the end of a heading or paragraph line: `# SALE {.invert .center}`
- on a span: `Total: [R$ 42,00]{.bold size=large}`
- on a line of their own: it applies to the **block above** (tables, images, objects): a table followed by `{.compact}`
- on a divider: `--- {.dashed thickness=2}`

| Class | Effect |
|---|---|
| `.left` `.center` `.right` `.justify` | alignment (justify spreads spaces on the character grid, or pixels in raster) |
| `.bold` `.italic` `.underline` `.strike` | style for the whole block or span |
| `.invert` | on a block: a **continuous** white-on-black band (raster); on a span: inverted words (native) |
| `.flip` | upside down (native `ESC {`, rows sent in reverse order; raster when a row is not native) |
| `.mono` | monospace (the printer font is already monospace) |
| `.compact` | tables: do not stretch |
| `.solid .dashed .dotted .double .wavy .cut` | divider style (`.cut` adds scissors: a place to tear) |

| Key | Effect | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `size=` | §5 | ✓ |
| `font=` | a role, alias or family name (§4) | ✓ |
| `align=` | same as the alignment classes | ✓ |
| `rotate=` | clockwise, like CSS: `90`, `180`, `270` exact; other angles allowed (nudge `B102`); always raster | ✓ |
| `render=raster\|native` | force how a block is printed (text blocks and QR codes) | ✓ |
| `thickness=` | divider stroke in dots (minimum 2, nudge `B101`) | ✓ |
| `leading=` | space between lines: `leading=18` dots, `18px` or `2mm`. Printer font: line height + N (`ESC 3`) | ✓ |
| `tracking=` | extra space after each character, in dots (≤ 32). Printer font: `ESC SP n`, doubled at 2× width on printers that follow the spec (not at 2× on the MTP-II: profile `native.tracking_unscaled_at`); line breaks use the real width | ✓ |
| `indent=` | left indent: `indent=4` columns, or `indent=3mm` / `24px`; wrapped lines stay aligned | ✓ |

Unknown classes or keys give `M101` and are ignored.

## 4. Fonts ✓

Three levels, from general to specific:

1. **Roles** in front matter — `body` (paragraphs, lists), `title` (headings), `code` (inline `code` in raster blocks).
2. **Aliases** — any other name in `fonts:` (`hand: Z003`), used with `{font=hand}` on a block or a span.
3. **Family names** — `{font="Atkinson Hyperlegible"}`.

`native` (the default for `body` and `title`) is the printer's internal font: fastest, sharpest, lightest on the
battery. Any other font makes that block raster. A native block with a raster span becomes raster too, drawn
with the printer-font look.

Fonts are looked up among the **bundled** fonts first (same result on every machine: Atkinson Hyperlegible,
IBM Plex Mono, Barlow Condensed, Terminus, Spleen, DejaVu Sans), then among installed fonts (fontconfig).
A font that cannot be found falls back to Atkinson Hyperlegible (`F203`).

Quality nudges, from the printed tests of the profile:
- below a font's **tested minimum** → `F201` with the minimum and the evidence;
- an **untested** font: bobina measures its stem at the requested size and warns below 2 dots (`F202`);
- inverted raster text thinner than bold 20 px → `F204`;
- a character the printer font lacks (emoji, arrows, `☐`) → that **line only** becomes raster (`F301`, a note);
  a character no font has → printed as a box (`F302`).

**Other scripts** (Thai, Indic, Khmer, Myanmar, Ethiopic, CJK): the first time a document needs one, bobina
downloads its Noto font (pinned URL, size and sha256; 38 KB for Thai, 4.5 to 8.3 MB for CJK), says so first (font,
OFL license, size, source; `F304`) and keeps it in `~/.local/share/bobina/fonts/` for offline use. No network, or
`bobina config set font_downloads off`: boxes and `F305` (`bobina fonts get thai`, a language or a document). Han
follows `lang:` (ja, ko, zh-TW), else nearby kana or hangul, else Simplified Chinese. These lines, and Arabic or
Hebrew ones, are drawn whole (joined, stacked, right to left), never letter by letter.

`bobina fonts test "FAMILY"` prints a size ladder; `bobina fonts mark "FAMILY" PX` records your minimum.

| Size at 203 dpi | Height | What works (tests F1, F2, R5) |
|---|---|---|
| < 12 px | < 1.5 mm | nothing legible |
| 12–13 px | ~1.5 mm | bitmap fonts made for it (Terminus, Spleen) |
| 14–19 px | ~2 mm | regular sans/mono with a large x-height (Atkinson) |
| ≥ 20 px | 2.5 mm | most fonts, serifs, thin weights, bold inverted text |
| ≥ 28 px | 3.5 mm | script and decorative fonts |

## 5. Sizes ✓

Named sizes are **physical**; the profile converts them with its `dpi`:

| Name | Height | 203 dpi | 300 dpi | Printer font (mtp-ii-58) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `small` | 1.5 mm | 12 px | 18 px | 1×1 |
| `normal` | 2.5 mm | 20 px | 30 px | 1×1 |
| `large` | 3.5 mm | 28 px | 41 px | 2×2 |
| `title` | 5 mm | 40 px | 59 px | 2×2 |
| `huge` | 8 mm | 64 px | 94 px | 3×3 |

Exact sizes: `size=20px` or `size=3mm` (raster fonts; the printer font uses the nearest multiplier, `F303`) and
printer multipliers `size=2x`, `size=1x2` (width × height; above 4× prints jagged).

## 6. Objects (fenced blocks)

The info string carries the object type and its attributes: ` ```qr {size=full .right} `.
Objects are centred unless aligned with `.left` / `.right`.

### 6.1 QR code ✓

````markdown
```qr {module=4 ecc=M}
https://example.com
```
````

`module=` dots per module (profile default 4; minimum 3 native, 4 raster → `Q101`), `ecc=L|M|Q|H` (`L` → `Q102`),
`size=full|half|third|30mm` — the largest **integer** module that fits (integer modules keep codes scannable;
native QR stops at 16), `render=raster`, `caption="Menu"` a centred line under the code. Content that does not fit
any QR → `Q109`, nothing printed.

### 6.2 Barcodes ✓

````markdown
```barcode {type=code128}
ABC-123
```
````

`type=code128` (default) `ean13 ean8 upca code39 code93 codabar itf` — native on the printer, with an exact
preview. `module=` (minimum 2), `height=` dots (default 80), `text=below|above|both|none`, `width=full`
(or `.justify`) stretches with the largest integer module (≤ 6). `orientation=auto|horizontal|vertical`:
`auto` turns a barcode wider than the paper into a **vertical** one along the paper, so it is never cut (`Q110`,
a warning, since you may not want it); vertical barcodes are raster with module ≥ 4 along the paper and a
10-module white margin (measured: 2 and 3 did not scan). CODE39 gets the firmware's mod-43 check character in the
bars (not in the text). 1–250 printable ASCII characters; types the profile does not support → `Q106`; weak types
(ITF) → `Q107`.

### 6.3 Payment codes (`pay`) ✓

````markdown
```pay {scheme=upi to="shop@okbank" name="Chai Point" amount=120 note="Order 42"}
```
````

One block for every payment scheme, with the same attributes: `to=` who receives, `name=`, `amount=` (`24.90` or
`24,90`, in the scheme's currency), `ref=` your reference, `note=` text for the payer; a few schemes take an extra
(`city=` Pix, `bic=` SEPA, `currency=` PayPal, `label=` other). `caption=auto|none|"text"`: `auto` prints a line
under the code with the scheme and the amount (`Pix · R$ 10,00`), or the name. The QR attributes (`size=`,
`module=`, `ecc=`) work too. Pix is one scheme like the others: `pay {scheme=pix to=… name=… city=…}` (the old
```` ```pix ```` block is gone: it prints as text with `M102` and the way to write it). Attributes take `{{ }}`, so
a receipt per row carries its own amount. Without `amount=` (or with 0) the code is open: the payer types it.

| Scheme | `to=` | Tested in the app |
|---|---|---|
| `pix` (Brazil, BR Code with CRC16) | Pix key: CPF/CNPJ (check digits verified), e-mail, +55 phone, random key | ✅ banking apps, 05/11 (CPF, e-mail, phone keys) |
| `upi` (India, `upi://pay`; `name=` required) | UPI ID (`shop@okbank`) | ⚠ not tested in a payment app |
| `epc` (SEPA / GiroCode, EPC069-12 v002; `name=` required) | IBAN (check digits verified) | ⚠ not tested in a payment app |
| `promptpay` (Thailand, EMVCo) | phone, 13-digit tax ID or e-wallet ID | ⚠ not tested in a payment app |
| `paynow` (Singapore, SGQR; `name=` required) | UEN or mobile (+65…) | ⚠ not tested in a payment app |
| `bitcoin` (BIP21) | address | ✅ a bitcoin wallet, 09/11 |
| `lightning` | BOLT11 invoice, LNURL or lightning address | ⚠ not tested in a payment app |
| `paypal` `revolut` `wise` `picpay` `mercadopago` | user name or the app's link | ✅ each app, 09/11 |
| `cashapp` `venmo` | `$cashtag` or user name | ⚠ not tested in a payment app |
| `other` (WeChat Pay, Alipay, DuitNow, Yape, QRIS…) | — the payload read from the app's own QR, in the block body | ⚠ reprinted unchecked |

A missing or invalid attribute (an IBAN with a wrong check digit, a UPI ID without `@`, more decimals than the
currency has) gives `Q111` with a working example, and the code is not printed: the rest of the document is, and
the command exits with 9 so a script or agent knows (`--allow Q111` for 0). A scheme nobody has scanned with its
real app gives the note `P302`; scan a print before customers use it (docs/TESTED.md). No brand logos (they need
a licence). What each field means in each scheme, its official name and its limit: `bobina help pay SCHEME`
(`--json` too) and [pay.md](docs/pay.md). A value over a limit is an error (`Q111` says how much to cut), never cut.
An amount that reads two ways (`amount=1.890`: R$ 1.890,00 or R$ 1,89?) is `Q111` too: write `1890`, `1.890,00` or `1.89`.
The same value in `| paymoney`, or in `| currency` without a locale (§7.1), is printed as typed with `M202`.

### 6.4 Data Matrix and PDF417 ✓

````markdown
```datamatrix {size=third}
batch 42
```

```pdf417 {module=2 columns=4}
long text
```
````

Raster (the printer has no native Data Matrix; its native PDF417 does not work). Data Matrix: `module=` (≥ 4),
`size=`. PDF417: `module=`, `ratio=`, `columns=`.

### 6.5 Images ✓

`![alt](photo.jpg){width=50% dither=atkinson gamma=1.5 .left}` or a fence ` ```image {…} ` with the path inside.

- Path relative to the document; `data:image/…;base64,…` embeds the image (≤ 10 MB).
- Formats: PNG, JPEG, GIF (first frame), WebP, BMP, TIFF; **SVG** and **PDF pages** (`page=N`, default 1) are
  rendered straight at the target width (extras `bobina[svg]`, `bobina[pdf]`; missing → `I105`). Vector sources
  default to `dither=threshold` (crisp line art); set `dither=` for photos inside a PDF.
- `https://` URLs only when the command line has `--allow-net` (`I103` otherwise); public hosts only,
  no redirects, ≤ 10 MB (`I106`); every fetch is reported (`I104`). A document cannot enable the network.
- `width=` dots or `%` (default: the paper width), `dither=floyd-steinberg|atkinson|bayer|threshold`,
  `gamma=` (defaults from front matter `image:`, then the profile — tuned on printed ramps).
- bobina looks at the ink (a plain background does not count): a drawing prints in black and white, a photo is
  dithered, and `I109` says which. `.dither` and `.threshold` choose; `threshold=60%` sets the cut.
- `rotate=90|180|270`, `.flip`, `.mirror` (left-right) turn the image before it is fitted to the paper.
- Images above 40 megapixels are refused (`I101`), unreadable ones give `I101` and the rest prints.

### 6.6 Text ✓

` ```text ` (or no type) prints the lines as they are, in the printer font, wrapping only lines wider than the paper
(`L103`). `rotate=90` turns the block. Any other language name (` ```python `) prints the same way with `M102`.

### 6.7 Raw bytes ✓

````markdown
```raw
1b 40   # hex bytes sent as-is; comments after #
```
````

The escape hatch: no checks, no preview (`P201`). Never accepted from variables (§7.4).

### 6.8 Contact codes (`contact`) ✓

````markdown
```contact whatsapp
+55 11 90000-0000
```
````

The network after `contact`; the value in the body: a phone with its country code, a user name or the app's link.
It prints a QR of the network's public link and a caption. `vcard` and `mecard` take `key: value` lines. A value
that makes no link is `Q112` (code left out, exit 9); every network gives `P303` until scanned with its app.
Networks and values: `bobina help contact` and [contact.md](docs/contact.md).

### 6.9 Planned objects ◇

` ```table {columns="auto,4ch,8ch" header=invert} ` (tables with explicit widths and styles), shapes and icons.

## 7. Variables (Jinja) ✓

The body is a **Jinja** template (the subset implemented by minijinja, so other languages can implement `bob/1`),
evaluated once in a **sandbox**: no files, no network, no imports. Comments are `<# … #>` (so `{#id}` stays a
Pandoc attribute).

Available: front-matter variables, template fields, `now` and `today` (time zone aware), `seq` (§7.3), `range`,
`namespace`, `label` (§8), and Jinja's built-in filters plus:

| Filter | Example (`locale: pt-BR`) |
|---|---|
| `date(style\|pattern)` | `{{ now \| date("full") }}` → quinta-feira, 5 de novembro de 2026 |
| `time`, `datetime` | `{{ now \| datetime("short") }}` → 05/11/2026 09:49 |
| `add(days=, hours=, minutes=, weeks=, months=, years=)` | `{{ now \| add(days=7) \| date("dd/MM") }}` → 12/11 |
| `currency(code)` | `{{ 1234.5 \| currency("BRL") }}` → R$ 1.234,50 |
| `number(decimals)`, `percent` | `{{ 1234.5 \| number }}` → 1.234,5 |
| `int`, `float` | `{{ "3 dias" \| int }}` → 3 |
| `letters` | `{{ 28 \| letters }}` → AB |
| `markdown` | interprets a value as Markdown (§7.4) |
| `upper`, `lower`, `capitalize`, `title`, `trim`, `truncate(n)`, `replace(a, b)` | Jinja's own: `{{ "arroz" \| upper }}` → ARROZ |
| `titlecase` | by the document language: `{{ "arroz DA fazenda" \| titlecase }}` → Arroz da Fazenda (`en`: Bread of the Day) |
| `deaccent` | `{{ "São João" \| deaccent }}` → Sao Joao |
| `camel`, `pascal`, `snake`, `kebab`, `slug` | `{{ "Arroz da Fazenda" \| snake }}` → arroz_da_fazenda (accents removed) |
| `smallcaps` | `{{ "Arroz" \| smallcaps }}` → Aʀʀᴏᴢ (Unicode small capitals: printed as an image line, `F301`; accented letters stay lowercase) |

Number filters read what a person types: `24.90`, `24,90`, `R$ 1.890,00`, `3 dias`. A value that is not a number
or is ambiguous (`1234.567`, `3 5`) gives `M202`: `currency`/`number`/`percent` print it as typed, `int`/`float`
give their default (0) and `add` counts it as 0, never a silent R$ 0,00. `percent` reads `10%` as 0.10.

Every filter keeps data as data: `{{ value | upper }}` from `--data`/`--set` is still printed literally and still
cannot become an image path (`M312`), and neither can a value joined into a path (`'img/' ~ value`).

### 7.1 Dates and languages

One locale for dates, numbers and money (`US$ 24,90`, `09/11/2026` in `pt-BR`): the document's `locale:`, else
`locale` in config.toml (`bobina config set locale TAG`), saved on first use from the time zone (`America/Sao_Paulo`:
`pt-BR`; `LANG`'s language if official there) or else a non-English `LANG`, said once (`M203`); else English
(`M204`). Only the document's `locale:` reads a typed `1.890` as a price (else `M202`); unknown: `M205`. No font
for the script (downloads off): English words, its country's formats (`en-TH`, `F306`).

Styles `short`, `medium`, `long`, `full` follow the document `locale` (the same line prints "Thursday, November 5,
2026" in `en-US`). Patterns use CLDR syntax (`dd/MM/yyyy HH:mm`); a pattern containing `%` is strftime, with month
and day names still localized. Moment.js tokens are not supported: `YYYY` and `DD` give `M201`.

### 7.2 Undefined variables

Printed as empty with `M130`.

### 7.3 Counters

A counter is an integer kept between prints; its appearance is formatting.

```yaml
counters:
  ticket: { start: 1, step: 1, format: "A-{:03}" }   # A-001, A-002 …  (one {:spec}, Python format)
  senha:  { format: "Senha {:d}" }                   # Senha 1, Senha 2 …  (the text goes in the format)
  box:    { start: 1, stop: 26, style: letters }     # A … Z, then M140 (wrap: true restarts)
  code:   { start: 255, style: hex }                 # FF, 100 …
```

| Write | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `{{ seq.ticket }}` | **one** value for the whole print (the same in the title and in the QR) |
| `{% for n in seq.ticket.take(10) %}` | ten new values in one print |
| `{% for n in range(1, 11) %}` | a local loop, not persisted |

Previews, `check` and `--dry-run` only show the next values; they take nothing. A print **reserves** its values when
it is built, so the confirmation screen shows the numbers that will be printed and two prints at the same time never
get the same number. If the job is then not printed (you quit, the printer is unreachable, the build fails), the
values go back, unless another print took numbers after them: then they stay skipped. A number is never printed
twice; a cancelled job may leave a gap (a job that stopped halfway also keeps its numbers; one you stop between
labels keeps those of the labels that printed). The CLI adds
`--repeat N` (N renders, new values each) and `--copies N` (identical copies); `bobina seq` lists and resets them,
and `bobina seq set NAME N` starts one at N, even before its first print.

### 7.4 Data is literal

**The author is trusted; data is not.** Values from `--data` (CSV), `--set` and any future server input:
- are inserted as **literal text** after Markdown parsing: `# PROMO` prints a hash, `{.invert}` prints braces;
- are never evaluated as templates;
- can never produce a `raw` block (`M314` for variables inside `raw`), choose an image path (`M312`), or carry
  control characters (removed from all text and barcode data before encoding).

`{{ value | markdown }}` opts one value in: its `raw` blocks are removed (`M121`), and for data values images too
(`M122`). Template violations are **errors**: files (`M310`), unsafe attributes (`M311`), more than 2000 loop
iterations or 2 MB of output (`M313`), template paths outside the document folder and
`~/.config/bobina/templates` (`M315`). See `docs/SECURITY.md`.

## 8. Templates ✓

A template is a `.bob.md` whose front matter declares its fields:

```yaml
---
fields:
  shop:  { required: true, example: "Padaria do Zé" }
  items: { required: true, type: table, columns: [item, qty, price] }
  pix:   { help: "Pix key: adds a Pix QR for the total" }
  date:  { default: "{{ now | datetime('short') }}" }
labels:
  en: { total: TOTAL, thanks: "Thank you!" }
  pt: { total: TOTAL, thanks: "Obrigado!" }
---
```

- `required: true` → empty gives `M131` (a warning in the confirmation screen); a `default:` may be an expression.
- `was: [old_name]` → a document that still uses a renamed field gets `M101` naming the new one.
- `labels` are picked by the document language (`{{ label.total }}`) and overridable with `labels:` in the document.
- Using one: `template: receipt` in front matter, the other keys are the fields. Lookup: a `.bob.md` path inside the
  document folder, `~/.config/bobina/templates/NAME.bob.md`, then the built-ins: `receipt` (items, total, optional
  Pix), `label`, `todo`, `card`, `note` and a gallery of shop tags (`bobina template list`; recipes in
  [guides/templates.md](docs/guides/templates.md)).
- `--ask` (on `print`, `check`, `preview`) asks the fields still missing on the terminal, in the order the
  template declares them, showing `help`, `example` and the default (`[automatic]` for expressions);
  `type: table` fields take one row per line (`item; qty; price`, empty line to finish). A document without
  `fields:` gets its undeclared `{{ variables }}` asked. Answers are data, exactly like `--set` (literal,
  never Markdown or template code); fields already set by the front matter, `--set` or `--data` columns are
  not asked; a required field left empty prints with `M131`. No terminal → usage error.
- `bobina template show NAME` lists the fields; `bobina template new NAME FILE` writes a starter with every field
  marked `# required` / `# optional`.

## 9. Rendering contract

- bobina decides every line break; the printer never wraps.
- Per line, native when the profile says the printer does it well, raster otherwise — a raster line looks like the
  native ones (the printer font is emulated); `render=` forces it.
- A print starts with the profile's top margin (fixes the faded start), separates blocks by `block_gap_dots`, and
  ends with enough feed for the last line to clear the tear bar with room to spare (profile `feed_after_dots`,
  or the printer's measured `tear_mm` + 6 mm; `tear_margin_mm` in the printer's config.toml changes the 6 mm).
- Errors stop a print only for parsing (`DOC`) and security (`M31x`); everything else is a nudge.

## Appendix A — nudge codes

Categories: **B** drawing · **F** fonts · **Q** codes · **L** layout · **I** images · **P** printer · **M** markup and
templates. `bobina help nudges` prints the same list; `allow: [CODE]` or `--allow CODE` silences one.


Errors (`E…`) stop the job: nothing prints. Exit codes are in `docs/CLI.md`.

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `E101` | error | command line usage |
| `E102` | error | this command takes one document |
| `E103` | error | a job option was given twice with different values |
| `E104` | error | --then / --compact misuse |
| `E105` | error | --last / --again misuse, or nothing printed yet |
| `E106` | error | only one part can read stdin |
| `E107` | error | a terminal is needed (confirmation or --ask) |
| `E201` | error | file not found or unreadable |
| `E202` | error | file type not supported as a target |
| `E203` | error | image, PDF page or page range not usable |
| `E204` | error | network target needs --allow-net |
| `E205` | error | nothing to print |
| `E206` | error | saved label (library) problem |
| `E207` | error | unknown template, profile, font or help topic |
| `E208` | error | output file problem (exists, format) |
| `E209` | error | a bobina state file is damaged or busy (counters, paper, library, config) |
| `E301` | error | data file unreadable or in an unsupported format |
| `E302` | error | no data rows (or none match --rows/--where) |
| `E303` | error | unknown column or sheet |
| `E304` | error | invalid value (--rows, --copies-from, --set, length) |
| `E305` | error | job too large (1000 labels, 100 copies) |
| `E401` | error | no printer configured or unknown printer |
| `E402` | error | printer unreachable |
| `E403` | error | printer not ready (paper, cover, error) |
| `E405` | error | printer busy: another bobina job kept it too long |
| `E406` | error | `bobina init` found no printer to set up |
| `E501` | error | document error |
| `E601` | error | no AI found, or an unknown AI name |
| `E602` | error | the AI did not answer |
| `E701` | error | could not check for a new bobina (`bobina update`) |

Nudges:

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `B101` | warning | stroke thinner than 2 dots prints broken |
| `B102` | note | free rotation angles look jagged |
| `F201` | warning | font below its tested minimum size |
| `F202` | warning | untested font with strokes thinner than 2 dots |
| `F203` | warning | font not found, a bundled font was used |
| `F204` | warning | inverted raster text too thin or small |
| `F205` | warning | font size out of range (6 to 400 px), clamped |
| `F301` | note | glyph not in the printer font: line printed as an image |
| `F302` | warning | glyph missing in every available font |
| `F303` | note | size not supported natively, nearest native size used |
| `F304` | note | font for another script downloaded (once; used offline from then on) |
| `F305` | warning | font for this script not downloaded (off, or no network): letters print as boxes |
| `F306` | note | no font for the locale's script (none, or downloads off): English words, its formats |
| `Q101` | warning | QR module too small to scan reliably |
| `Q102` | warning | QR error correction L reads with difficulty |
| `Q103` | warning | QR wider than the paper |
| `Q104` | warning | barcode wider than the paper |
| `Q105` | note | barcode preview is approximate (no encoder for this type) |
| `Q106` | warning | barcode type not supported by this printer |
| `Q107` | warning | barcode type prints but phones struggle to read it |
| `Q108` | warning | barcode module too thin to scan |
| `Q109` | warning | invalid barcode content |
| `Q110` | warning | barcode turned vertical to fit the paper |
| `Q111` | warning | payment code not built: an attribute is missing or invalid (the code is left out, the rest prints, exit 9) |
| `Q112` | warning | contact code not built: the network or its value is wrong (left out, exit 9) |
| `L101` | warning | word longer than the line was split |
| `L102` | note | long print |
| `L103` | warning | preformatted line longer than the paper was wrapped |
| `L104` | warning | rotated block wider than the paper was cropped |
| `L105` | warning | nothing printable: every block was skipped |
| `I101` | warning | image not found, unreadable or in an unsupported format (the hint lists the formats) |
| `I102` | note | image downscaled to the paper width |
| `I103` | warning | network image skipped: fetching shows the server when you print, and a shared document could reach your local network; add `--allow-net` if you trust it |
| `I104` | note | image fetched from the network (the server sees the print) |
| `I105` | warning | PDF/SVG support not installed |
| `I106` | warning | network source refused (private address, redirect, type, size) |
| `I107` | warning | `![](a b.png)` is not an image (path with a space): write `![](<a b.png>)` |
| `I108` | warning | image outside its folder and `image_dirs` (`--sandbox`, MCP) |
| `I109` | note | an image read as a drawing (black and white) or a photo (dithered) |
| `P101` | warning | the paper roll is almost over (estimate) |
| `P102` | warning | the print is longer than the paper left on the roll (estimate) |
| `P103` | warning | the roll is not as wide as this printer's paper (`paper new --width`; recorded anyway) |
| `P104` | note | roll length not set: no paper estimate |
| `P105` | note | `--compact`: labels print at once, without stops |
| `P106` | note | `--step` without a terminal: labels print at once |
| `P201` | warning | raw bytes bypass every check and are not previewed |
| `P301` | note | this job uses a feature not tested on paper yet |
| `P302` | note | a payment code nobody has scanned with its app yet |
| `P303` | note | a contact code nobody has scanned with its app yet |
| `P401` | note | no Bluetooth or USB search here (says why) |
| `P402` | note | the name does not settle the profile: one was taken |
| `P403` | warning | a USB printer this user cannot write to |
| `P404` | warning | config.toml names a profile bobina does not know |
| `M101` | warning | unknown attribute |
| `M102` | note | unknown block type, printed as preformatted text |
| `M103` | note | attribute not implemented yet (ignored) |
| `M120` | note | field rendered as Markdown |
| `M121` | warning | raw block removed from a variable |
| `M122` | warning | image removed from a --data/--set value |
| `M130` | warning | undefined variable printed as empty |
| `M131` | warning | required template field is empty |
| `M140` | warning | counter passed its stop value |
| `M150` | warning | `--join`: rows of the main source without a match (their joined fields print empty) |
| `M151` | warning | `--join`: the joined source repeats a key (the first row is used) |
| `M152` | warning | `--join`: a column exists in two sources; `{{ col }}` uses the main one, `{{ b.col }}` the other |
| `M153` | warning | data values lost: a row with more fields than the header, or values under an empty header |
| `M154` | warning | the data header repeats a column name (the last one is used) |
| `M155` | note | a data source was renamed because a column has its name (`produto.csv` with a `produto` column → `produto_src`) |
| `M156` | note | an option has no effect here (`--sheet` on a CSV, `--repeat` with `--data`) |
| `M157` | warning | `--set` replaces a data column of the same name in every row (decided: what you type wins) |
| `M158` | note | data columns renamed to names usable in `{{ }}`: `Product Name` → `product_name`, `Preço` → `preco`; `{{ row['Product Name'] }}` keeps the exact name |
| `M159` | warning | two data columns would get the same usable name; the first keeps it |
| `M160` | note | Excel formula cells without a saved value print empty |
| `M201` | warning | date pattern looks like Moment.js |
| `M202` | warning | a value is not a number, or a date moved out of the calendar (printed as it is) |
| `M203` | note | this machine's locale, from its time zone, saved in config.toml (said once) |
| `M204` | note | no locale for this machine: dates, numbers and money in English |
| `M205` | warning | the document's locale: is not a locale bobina knows (the machine's is used) |
| `M310` | error | templates cannot read files |
| `M311` | error | unsafe template operation |
| `M312` | error | a variable cannot choose a file path |
| `M313` | error | template limit exceeded |
| `M314` | error | variables cannot be used inside raw blocks |
| `M315` | error | template path outside the allowed folders |
