<!-- file: docs/guides/batch-printing.md -->

# Printing a batch: one label per row

You have **one label design** and **a list of things** to label: jars in the pantry, guests at a party, products
on a shelf, kids' school notebooks. Instead of editing and printing the label once per item, you write the design
once with blanks, put the list in a table, and bobina prints one label per row.

```
  the design (with blanks)          the list (one row per label)          what prints
 ┌──────────────────────┐     ┌─────────────┬────────────┬───────┐     ┌──────────────┐
 │   {{ product }}      │     │ product     │ packed     │ shelf │     │  Brown rice  │
 │ - - - - - - - - - -  │  +  ├─────────────┼────────────┼───────┤  =  │  Packed …  A │
 │ Packed {{ packed }}  │     │ Brown rice  │ 2026-11-07 │ A     │     ├──────────────┤
 │ Shelf {{ shelf }}    │     │ Black beans │ 2026-11-07 │ A     │     │ Black beans  │
 └──────────────────────┘     │ Coffee      │ 2026-11-01 │ B     │     │  Packed …  A │
                              └─────────────┴────────────┴───────┘     ├──────────────┤
                                                                       │    Coffee    │
                                                                       └──────────────┘
```

The **column names of the table are the names of the blanks**. That is the whole idea. The files of this guide
are in [`examples/batch/`](examples/batch): run the commands from that folder.

## 1. The design, with blanks

`jar-label.bob.md` is an ordinary bobina document. Each `{{ name }}` is a blank:

```markdown
---
fields:
  product: { required: true, example: "Brown rice" }
  packed:  { help: "date the jar was filled (YYYY-MM-DD)" }
  best_before: { help: "YYYY-MM-DD; leave empty if it does not expire" }
  shelf:   { example: "A" }
---
# {{ product }} {.center}

--- {.dashed}

Packed **{{ packed }}** {.center}
{% if best_before %}

Best before **{{ best_before }}** {.center}
{% endif %}

Shelf {{ shelf }} {.center}
```

The `fields:` list at the top is optional. It documents the blanks (`bobina template show`), marks the
required ones, and lets `--ask` ask for them. `{% if best_before %}` skips that line when the value is empty.

**Try it with one label first**, filling the blanks by hand:

```sh
bobina preview jar-label.bob.md --set product="Brown rice" --set packed=2026-11-07 \
  --set best_before=2027-05-07 --set shelf=A -o one.png
```

![one label](examples/batch/one.png)

Or let bobina ask: `bobina print jar-label.bob.md --ask`.

## 2. The list, as a table

The same list in three formats. Use whichever you already have; bobina reads them all with `--data`.

**A spreadsheet** (`pantry.xlsx`, first sheet, or `--sheet Pantry`): the first filled row is the header.

| product | packed | best_before | shelf | jars |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Brown rice | 2026-11-07 | 2027-05-07 | A | 2 |
| Black beans | 2026-11-07 | 2027-11-07 | A | 1 |
| Coffee | 2026-11-01 | 2027-02-01 | B | 1 |
| Salt | 2026-10-20 | | B | 0 |

**CSV** (`pantry.csv`), what a spreadsheet saves with "Save as CSV". Commas, semicolons, tabs or `|` all work:

```csv
product,packed,best_before,shelf,jars
Brown rice,2026-11-07,2027-05-07,A,2
Black beans,2026-11-07,2027-11-07,A,1
Coffee,2026-11-01,2027-02-01,B,1
Salt,2026-10-20,,B,0
```

**JSON** (`pantry.json`), what a program or a web service usually gives you: a list of objects, one per label,
with the blank names as keys.

```json
[
  { "product": "Brown rice",  "packed": "2026-11-07", "best_before": "2027-05-07", "shelf": "A", "jars": 2 },
  { "product": "Black beans", "packed": "2026-11-07", "best_before": "2027-11-07", "shelf": "A", "jars": 1 },
  { "product": "Coffee",      "packed": "2026-11-01", "best_before": "2027-02-01", "shelf": "B", "jars": 1 },
  { "product": "Salt",        "packed": "2026-10-20", "best_before": "",           "shelf": "B", "jars": 0 }
]
```

Columns that the design does not use (here `jars`) are simply ignored, unless you use them for copies (step 4).

## 3. Preview the whole batch, then print

```sh
bobina preview jar-label.bob.md --data pantry.csv -o all.png   # look first
bobina print   jar-label.bob.md --data pantry.csv              # confirmation screen, then p
```

![four labels, one per row](examples/batch/all.png)

Four rows, four labels, one print job. Salt has no `best_before`, so that line is not printed.

## 4. Only some rows, and copies per row

| You want | Add | With this list |
|---|---|---|
| only rows 2 to 3 | `--rows 2-3` | Black beans, Coffee |
| only shelf A | `--where shelf=A` | Brown rice, Black beans |
| everything except salt | `--where product!=salt` | the first three |
| names containing "rice" | `--where product~=rice` | Brown rice |
| as many labels as jars | `--copies-from jars` | rice ×2, beans ×1, coffee ×1, salt skipped (0) |

Filters combine. Shelf A, one label per jar:

```sh
bobina print jar-label.bob.md --data pantry.json --where shelf=A --copies-from jars
```

![shelf A, one label per jar](examples/batch/shelfA.png)

`--rows` counts data rows (1 is the first row after the header) and is applied before `--where`. Matching ignores
upper/lower case. A column name that does not exist stops with the list of columns that do.

## 5. Two sources for one label (`--join`)

Sometimes the label needs columns from two places: prices in a spreadsheet, the catalog (category, id) in a
JSON exported by another system. Name the sources and say which column matches them:

```sh
bobina print shelf-tag.bob.md --data a=prices.xlsx --join b=catalog.json --on name
```

| `prices.xlsx` (a) | | | | `catalog.json` (b) | | |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| name | price | size | category | name | category | id |
| Rice | 12.5 | 1kg | grains | rice | grocery | 101 |
| Salt | 3 | 1kg | spice | | | |

In the design, a column without a prefix works when only one source has it; the prefix picks one when both do:

```markdown
{{ name }} — {{ price }} ({{ size }})       ← name is the key; price and size only exist in a
{{ id }}                                    ← only in b
{{ a.category }}{% if b.category %} / {{ b.category }}{% endif %}   ← both have it: the prefix chooses
```

- `--data` is the **main** source: one label per row. `--join` adds the columns of the row with the same key
  (matching ignores upper/lower case). Without a name, a source is called after its file (`catalog.json` →
  `{{ catalog.id }}`).
- Different key names: `--on name=product`. Several joins: each `--on` belongs to the `--join` before it
  (`--join b=catalog.json --on name --join stock.csv --on b.id=id`).
- Rows without a match print with the joined fields empty, and one warning lists them (`M150`); guard what
  surrounds a joined field so it does not dangle: `{% if b.category %} / {{ b.category }}{% endif %}`. A key repeated
  in the joined source uses its first row (`M151`); `{{ category }}` in both sources uses the main one and says
  so (`M152`). `--where`, `--rows` and `--copies-from` work after the join, also on joined columns
  (`--where b.category=grocery`).
- Values from every source are printed literally, and only the command line chooses the files.

## Column names

A blank in the design is written like a variable: letters, digits and `_`. Headers that are not written that way
get a usable name automatically (and a note lists them): `Product Name` → `product_name`, `Preço` → `preco`,
`Data de Validade` → `data_de_validade`. The exact header always works too: `{{ row['Product Name'] }}`. If two
headers would get the same name, the first keeps it and a warning says so (`M159`).

## Good to know

- **Values are printed exactly as written.** A product called `**NEW** {{ x }}` prints those characters; data
  never becomes formatting, template code or printer commands. Only the design decides the layout.
- **Empty values**: a blank with no value prints empty (`M130`); a required one gives `M131` with the data row
  (`data row 3: required field 'product' is empty`). `--strict` stops the job instead.
- **`--set` and a column with the same name**: `--set` wins in every row (`M157`), handy to fix one field for
  the whole batch. `--where`, `--rows`, `--copies-from` and `--sheet` need `--data`; two `--data` in one part is
  an error (use `--then` to print both lists, `--join` to combine them). Both are warnings
  on the confirmation screen; nothing is blocked.
- **Spreadsheets**: formulas are not recalculated; the value Excel saved is used. `.xls`/`.ods` must be saved as
  `.xlsx` or `.csv`. Dates come out as `YYYY-MM-DD` (format them in the design with `{{ packed | date }}`).
- **Paper**: each label ends at the tear bar and bobina waits while you tear it off (`--no-step`: all at once).
  `--compact` prints one strip with ✂ lines and one feed at the end; `--then other.bob.md` adds to it.
- **Limits**: 1000 labels per job, copies included (`--copies`, `--copies-from`, `--repeat`, every `--then` part),
  and at most 100 copies of one label. Split bigger lists with `--rows`. `--copies` and `--copies-from` multiply.
- **Saved designs**: `bobina library add jar jar-label.bob.md`, then `bobina print @jar --data pantry.csv`.

## Other ideas

| Design | List |
|---|---|
| name badge (`{{ name }}`, `{{ company }}`) | the guest list exported from a form |
| shipping label (`{{ name }}`, `{{ address }}`, a QR with `{{ tracking }}`) | the day's orders as CSV |
| price tag (`{{ product }}`, `{{ price | currency('BRL') }}`, a barcode with `{{ ean }}`) | the price spreadsheet |
| school labels (`{{ child }}`, `{{ subject }}`) | one row per notebook, `--copies-from` for spares |


<!-- file: docs/guides/templates.md -->

# Ready-made templates: recipes and gallery

A template is a document with blanks that ships with bobina. You give it the values; it does the layout. Every
template below prints on a 58 mm roll with no warning.

```bash
bobina template list                          # every template and its fields
bobina template show label                    # one template: fields, required, examples
bobina template new label box.bob.md          # a starter file with every field, marked required / optional
bobina preview box.bob.md -o box.png          # look before printing
bobina print box.bob.md                       # confirmation screen, then paper
```

A document uses a template with `template: NAME` in its front matter; **the other keys are the fields**. A field
can also come from `--set NAME=VALUE`, `--ask` (asked on the terminal) or a column of `--data` (one label per row,
see [batch-printing.md](docs/guides/batch-printing.md)). `locale: pt-BR` switches the template's fixed words and the date
format to Portuguese (without it: the machine's, `bobina config get locale`). The full rules are in [FORMAT.md §8](docs/FORMAT.md).

## Recipe: a box label (`label`)

A big inverted title, lines under it and an optional Code 128 or QR code: a box, a shelf, a jar.

```markdown
---
template: label
locale: pt-BR
title: "FRÁGIL"
lines: ["Este lado para cima", "Manusear com cuidado"]
barcode: "PED-1042"
---
```

![label](spec/conformance/templates-label.png)

- `title` is required; `lines` is a list (one centred line each); `qr` instead of `barcode` for a link or a
  Pix key.
- One label per item of a list: keep the design, move the values to a CSV and print with `--data items.csv`.

## Recipe: a card (`card`)

A title between wavy rules, a message that may use Markdown (`**bold**`), a signature on the right.

```markdown
---
template: card
locale: pt-BR
title: "Feliz aniversário!"
message: "Que o seu ano seja **leve** e cheio de boas notícias."
from: "Ana e Pedro"
---
```

![card](spec/conformance/templates-card.png)

- `title` and `message` are required; without `from` there is no signature line.
- From the terminal, without a file: `bobina edit --template card` opens a draft in your editor.

## Recipe: a to-do list (`todo`)

A heading, today's date written out, one checkbox per item. An item that starts with `x ` is printed done.

```markdown
---
template: todo
locale: pt-BR
title: "Mercado"
items: ["arroz", "x feijão", "café", "pão francês"]
---
```

![todo](spec/conformance/templates-todo.png)

- `items` is required; `title` defaults to "To do" ("Tarefas" in Portuguese); `date` defaults to today, so a
  list printed on Monday says Monday.
- Leave `items` out of the file and pass `--ask`: bobina asks for the items on the terminal.

## Gallery: one template per kind of shop

Each one is a small document in [`examples/templates/`](examples/templates), printed here as it comes out of
the printer. Copy one, change the values, print.

| Shop | Template | What it has | Preview |
|---|---|---|---|
| Clothing | `clothing-tag` | brand, piece, size and colour, price, SKU as Code 128 | ![](examples/templates/clothing-tag.png) |
| Grocery | `shelf-price` | product, a huge price, price per kg or L, EAN-13 | ![](examples/templates/shelf-price.png) |
| Grocery | `sale-price` | an inverted SALE band, the old price struck through, the new price | ![](examples/templates/sale-price.png) |
| Kitchen | `food-label` | product inverted, made today, use by today + `days` (default 3), storage, who, batch | ![](examples/templates/food-label.png) |
| Jewellery | `jewelry-tag` | piece, code, metal and weight, price; short lines for a narrow strip | ![](examples/templates/jewelry-tag.png) |
| Online shop | `shipping-label` | recipient and address in large type, sender, order, tracking as Code 128 | ![](examples/templates/shipping-label.png) |
| Any counter | `pay-sign` | "Pay with …" and a big payment code for any scheme (Pix, UPI, SEPA…), the name, the amount or "any amount" | ![](examples/templates/pay-sign.png) |

- A price can be typed `24.90`, `24,90` or `R$ 1.890,00`; the template writes it in the currency of `currency`
  (default `BRL`, `R$ 24,90` in Portuguese). A price that is not a number (`consulte`) or is ambiguous
  (`1234.567`) prints as typed, with `M202`. A `days` the food label cannot count (`uma semana`) counts as 0, so
  the use-by date is today, also with `M202`: look at the warning before printing.
- `food-label` computes both dates when it prints: the same file printed tomorrow says tomorrow. Print a batch
  on the day it is made; `print --last` reprints the identical bytes, old dates included.
- Price tags for a whole shelf come from a spreadsheet: `bobina print shelf-price.bob.md --data prices.xlsx`,
  one column per field.

## Your own templates

A template is a `.bob.md` with a `fields:` front matter (FORMAT.md §8). Put it in `~/.config/bobina/templates/`
and `template: my-price` finds it; one with the same name as a built-in one wins over it. A `.bob.md` path next
to the document works too (`template: tags/price.bob.md`). The built-in ones are in
[`src/bobina/templates/`](src/bobina/templates): copy one and change its layout. `bobina template list`
shows only the built-in ones.


<!-- file: docs/SECURITY.md -->

# Security model

Status: threat model and defenses for v0.x; red teams in `tests/test_security*.py`.

## What bobina is

A local CLI. It reads a document, renders it, and — after a confirmation — sends bytes to a printer.
`bobina mcp` runs every document in `--sandbox`; a print server is planned (below).

## Trust boundaries

| Principal | Trust | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| The person at the terminal | trusted | flags, `~/.config/bobina/config.toml`, `--editor`, printer `command` |
| Document author | trusted for layout and the images it names, **not** for templates outside its folder | a `.bob.md` you wrote, or one somebody shared |
| Data | **untrusted** | `--data` CSV cells, `--set` values, future server/chat input |
| Template from elsewhere | like a document | built-ins, `~/.config/bobina/templates/`, the document folder |

## Assets

Local files (photos, notes, keys), the printer's configuration (command language, settings reachable
with vendor commands), paper and battery, counters, and the history of the last print.

## Defenses

| Threat | Defense | Test |
|---|---|---|
| Data changes structure (`# PROMO`, `{.invert}`, `**x**`) | every `{{ }}` is a placeholder, substituted as literal text after parsing | `test_templating.py` |
| Data evaluated as template (`{{ seq.x.take(500) }}`) | values are never re-evaluated | `test_data_is_never_evaluated_as_template` |
| Data emits printer commands | no `raw` from data (`M314`, `RAW_FENCE` in `| markdown`); C0/C1 controls stripped from all text and barcode data | `test_no_path_lets_data_emit_raw_bytes`, `test_control_characters_never_reach_the_printer` |
| Data chooses a file to print/preview | image paths with data are refused (`M312`); `| markdown` on data removes images and image fences (`M122`) | `test_data_cannot_*` |
| Shared document pulls files via `template:` | template paths must be inside the document folder or `~/.config/bobina/templates` (`M315`) | `test_template_path_outside_document_folder_is_refused` |
| Template escapes the sandbox | Jinja `ImmutableSandboxedEnvironment`, no loader (`include`/`import` → `M310`), unsafe attributes → `M311`, globals cleared except `now`, `today`, `seq`, `range`, `namespace`, `label` | `test_sandbox_blocks` |
| Paper/CPU exhaustion | 2000 loop steps, 10 000 macro calls, 10 s, values and output ≤ 2 MB (`M313`), 1000 renders / 100 copies per batch, nudge above 30 cm, **confirmation before every print** | `test_sandbox_blocks`, `test_security_limits.py` |
| Spreadsheets (`--data .xlsx`) | formulas never evaluated (cached values only), file ≤ 20 MB, unpacked ≤ 200 MB (zip bomb), first 10 000 rows read; `.xls`/`.ods` refused; every value literal | `test_xlsx_values_sheet_and_no_formulas` |
| Image bombs | `Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS = 40M`; base64 images and downloads ≤ 10 MB; PDF/SVG renders ≤ 8000 dots tall | `test_decompression_bomb_is_refused` |
| Image parsers as attack surface | Pillow limited to PNG/JPEG/GIF/BMP/WebP/TIFF (no EPS → no Ghostscript); PDF: one page rendered; SVG: `DOCTYPE`/`ENTITY` refused | `test_eps_is_not_opened`, `test_svg_with_entities_is_refused` |
| Shared document reads any image | `--sandbox` (MCP: always): only its folder and `image_dirs`, after symlinks (`I108`) | `test_sandbox` |
| SVG reads local files | every `href`/`url()` that is not `#fragment` or inline PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP is removed before rendering (resvg would load absolute paths) | `test_svg_external_references_are_removed` |
| Document makes requests (tracking, SSRF into localhost/LAN/tailnet) | network images off unless the **command line** says `--allow-net` (`I103`); https only; every resolved address must be public (no loopback, private, link-local, CGNAT/tailnet, multicast; IPv4 in IPv6 checked) and the connection goes to the checked address (no rebinding); no redirects; image/PDF content types only; 10 MB / 10 s; each fetch is reported (`I104`) | `test_network_is_off_by_default`, `test_private_addresses_are_refused` |
| Malformed codes | barcode 1–250 printable ASCII; QR overflow; Pix key ≤ 77 chars, numeric amount, TLV ≤ 99 → nudge `Q109`, no crash | `test_oversized_or_invalid_codes_*` |
| Counter format strings | only one `{:spec}` allowed (`FMT_RE`), no attribute access | — |
| Font lookups | `fc-match` without a shell; the result must match the requested family | — |
| Fonts for other scripts (Thai, CJK…) | a document can make bobina download one, once: only the files pinned in `scriptfonts.py` (https at a fixed notofonts / Google Fonts commit, exact size and sha256, no redirects, 12 MB), written atomically. Reveals to GitHub that some text needs that script; `font_downloads = false` turns it off (`F305`, boxes) | `test_scriptfonts.py` |

Raw blocks written by the **author** are allowed by design (escape hatch): they always raise `P201`
in the confirmation screen and are never previewed. A shared document with a `raw` block can switch
the printer's command language on models that support it (`bobina mode esc` restores it; the MTP-II ignores it).

## Privacy

- The last print (source, bytes, preview) is kept in `~/.local/state/bobina/last/` for `print --last`.
  It can contain personal data (Pix keys, names). `bobina config set keep_last off` disables it.
- Drafts live in `~/.local/state/bobina/drafts/`.

<!-- 'Requirements before a print server or chat bot exists' left out here: see docs/SECURITY.md -->

<!-- 'Open' left out here: see docs/SECURITY.md -->


<!-- file: docs/INSTALL.md -->

# Installing bobina

bobina needs Python 3.11 or newer. Pick one way:

| You have | Run |
|---|---|
| Linux or macOS, nothing set up | `curl -LsSf https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rafaelbressan/bobina/main/get.sh \| sh` |
| uv | `uv tool install bobina` |
| Debian 12+, Ubuntu 24.04+ | the .deb (below), or `sudo apt install pipx && pipx ensurepath && pipx install bobina` |
| Homebrew (macOS) | `brew tap rafaelbressan/bobina https://github.com/rafaelbressan/bobina && brew install rafaelbressan/bobina/bobina` |
| Windows | `uv tool install bobina` or `pipx install bobina` (printer driver: `drivers/windows/`) |
| A checkout, to change bobina | `./install.sh` (editable install, plus the Bluetooth service on Linux) |

Then `bobina init` (printer, profile, locale, roll, a test strip).

## Upgrading

`bobina update` shows the upgrade command of whatever installed bobina (uv, pipx, pip, Homebrew) and asks before
running it; for the .deb and git installs it says the steps. `--check` exits 10 when a release is newer. Once a
day a command at a terminal ends with `bobina 0.1.4 is available (you have 0.1.3): uv tool upgrade bobina`, never
for agents, scripts or pipes (`bobina config set update_check off`).

## Bluetooth needs the system Python

bobina talks to Bluetooth printers through RFCOMM sockets (`socket.AF_BLUETOOTH`), which only Linux has and
only a Python built with the BlueZ headers provides. Debian's and Ubuntu's `python3` have them; the Pythons that uv
downloads and Homebrew's do not (checked on uv 0.13 and Homebrew 7). Without them a Bluetooth printer fails with
"was built without Bluetooth sockets", which says how to reinstall; file (`--path`) and command (`--command`, e.g. ssh to the host with
the printer) printers work everywhere.

- The .deb and pipx from apt use the system Python; `get.sh` picks one with Bluetooth sockets, or says there is none.
- By hand: `uv tool install --reinstall --python /usr/bin/python3 bobina` (also moves an install off uv's Python).
- Ubuntu 22.04 has Python 3.10: `sudo apt install python3.11`, then `pipx install --python python3.11 bobina`.
- Pairing and the boot service need BlueZ: `sudo apt install bluez`.

## get.sh

`get.sh` installs uv with its official installer when it is missing, then runs `uv tool install bobina`.
Running it again upgrades and keeps the extras installed before. Options go after `sh -s --`:

```bash
curl -LsSf https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rafaelbressan/bobina/main/get.sh | sh -s -- --bluetooth-service
```

| Option | What |
|---|---|
| `--bluetooth-service` | Linux: the systemd user service `bt-printer.service`: Bluetooth on and the printer paired at boot. Its files come from the git tag of the installed version, into `~/.local/share/bobina/` |
| `--extras pdf,svg,xlsx,mcp` | optional parts: PDF pages, SVG images, `.xlsx` data, `bobina mcp` (the server for agents) |
| `--version 0.2.0` | that version instead of the latest (`0.2.0rc1` for a pre-release) |
| `--python PATH` | the Python to install with |

Uninstall: `uv tool uninstall bobina`; the service: `systemctl --user disable bt-printer.service`, then delete
`~/.config/systemd/user/bt-printer.service` and `~/.local/share/bobina/`.

## Debian and Ubuntu: the .deb

Each [release](https://github.com/rafaelbressan/bobina/releases) has `bobina_X.Y.Z_amd64.deb` and `_arm64.deb`
(64-bit Raspberry Pi OS too): `sudo apt install ./bobina_X.Y.Z_arm64.deb`. It runs on the system `python3` (3.11
to 3.14) with its own copies of the dependencies, not Debian's. No apt repository (`bobina update` says the next
.deb) and no extras: for them, pipx from apt (above).

## Homebrew

This repository is the tap; install with the full name (Homebrew 7 trusts a tap only then). No extras (`pdf`,
`svg`, `xlsx`, `mcp`): for them, `get.sh --extras`. No Bluetooth sockets (above): on Linux prefer `get.sh` or the
.deb.
